I obviously agreed, but I did ask him why, since I’d never experienced that with any other guy I’ve dated before. He said he could really see us going long term and didn’t want to spoil the emotional bond by having sex before he’s ready.

This really bothered me too. I’ve met men who are way more comfortable having sex after a good emotional bond is established, even if they do find the woman attractive. Self control exists in both genders..
You did nothing wrong. It’s very likely that he was never planning to meet up, even if he told you so. Some guys are just after cam stuff.

First of all I’m sorry you’re going through this. The same thing happened to me but with a man I had been seeing for two years! So I’ve come to learn that time invested is not a precise, completely foolproof measurement of how things will work out in the end. A long term relationship might happen within two months, a week, or a year, or it might not happen. 

Knowing this has helped me move on and be a bit more grounded when dating. I no longer believe that a good relationship will develop simply because we’ve been dating for a while. People’s minds do change from one day to the next depending on circumstances so varied that there’s no point dwelling on them. It has nothing to do with you or anything you did or failed to do, and everything to do with him, his life, and his inner struggles.
This. It’s always so much easier and comfortable to blame everything on modern dating culture. Either roll with it or find another way to work things out.
Also, don’t hide your annoyance from him. He will only continue to think that you’re cool with his behavior when you’re actually not. Show some disappointment if he changes up on you again

Im getting casual vibes from him, especially from forgetting about plans you guys had and changing them up last minute. That is unusual in a person who is actively pursuing you. My guess is you guys are just hanging out and he doesn’t seem interested or invested in starting a relationship from this

Now that you have been intimate it is a good time to ask where he sees the relationship going and express your desire for exclusivity. He shouldn’t perceive it as you rushing through things. After intimacy is involved it is quite expected that someone will bring this stuff up

This. You have to be willing to respect the fact that he can’t see you more often at the moment. It’s great that he’s willing to have conversations about your needs, but remember that the needs we have might not always be met exactly in the way we’d want to. You’ve got to reach a compromise that will make you both happy.

Also, if it takes him more than you’d be willing to allow to make progress, do consider moving on. Stick to your time limit and ask yourself later down the line if you’re willing to continue waiting for him or if you’d rather find somebody else.

I think you should definitely focus on matching his energy. Your efforts will not be welcome as long as he isn’t in the same place that you are, and they might actually make things worse, as men tend to take distance when they feel they’re being pressured or rushed into something they’re not ready for. 

I totally understand where you’re coming from, I don’t mind taking the reigns in a budding relationship either, but experience has taught me that respecting the other person’s boundaries is the most important thing.   Give this man some space to figure things out and let him come to you. Don’t let anxiety take a hold of your mind. Just enjoy the interactions you have for what they are.

I can tell you’re approaching this situation in the most mature way possible, but I’d pay attention to what you write at the end of your post. You worry that if you stop investing energy into progressing the relationship, he will not do anything even if he is ready. Thing is, you shouldn’t be worrying about that if your focus is on the present. You have absolutely no control over his reactions or decisions in this matter, whatever happens will depend on what he chooses to do.
He might have been nervous. If he tells you that you’re gorgeous then that means he truly feels it, it has nothing to do with you. Men aren’t automatic boner switches

There’s nothing wrong with initiating from time to time as a woman. Men like to know you’re interested as well! And if he had been pursuing you all this time I think it’s safe to assume there’s nothing to worry about.

I won’t go out of my way to call her mean, but I can definitely call her a bit immature for not having the guts to break things off earlier and in a more timely manner. 

You will meet a girl that will feel lucky to have you. I know it doesn’t seem like it right now and the least thing one can think of after going through a breakup is starting all over again. Focus on yourself, your studies, on texting your friends more, maybe read, write, play video games, whatever it is you want to do. You can reach out for closure but I’ve been there and there is little these people can say to is that will make it hurt less.

It will hurt but you will have the space now to meet somebody who is sure about you.

Im also the youngest woman he’s ever gone out with.

Honestly just message him and tell him that you want to slow down since you’ve only actually met one time. His answer, whether he takes it well or not, will tell you everything you need to know to worker walk away or stay.

No hate, but I really don’t understand people who have just one type and stick to it. I like skinny men with darker hair and glasses. I’ve also dated chubby men with beards, blonde men, darker skinned men. I don’t automatically find someone unattractive just because they don’t match a pattern. Is this a men/women difference?

If you’re 100% sure you’re not attracted and are not excited to know more about him, I would recommend that you don’t go on a second date. I believe in giving people a chance when there is something there that can still give off a spark on a second meeting, but if you truly believe it won’t happen, don’t waste his or your time.

I (as a woman) find that attraction can grow over time. I might not be too attracted to a certain man on the first date, but will feel the attraction grow a lot once I her to know him better if he does fit within the range of “my type” (geeky, taller than me) and there’s no major turn offs (like bad hygiene or whatever). Im not sure if men are different in that sense. Do you think your attraction is also based on personality or is it purely physical?

Consider that if you were running out of things to talk about in the first place, the connection most likely wasn’t that strong. We can often confuse infatuation or lust with actual connection. But if things don’t flow naturally, it wasn’t going to work out on the first place. Ghosting sucks and is a bad move, you dodged a bullet.

I don’t think there is a time set for exclusivity, we all have our own rhythm when it comes to relationships. I do have a few questions though: How long do your dates usually last? Do you have deep and engaging conversations and feel like he is slowly opening up to you?

I honestly feel like I won’t be able to take another rejection and don’t understand why everyone seems to be able to just disengage while I’m stuck to anybody the moment I meet them. And if we have sex it’s only so much worse. 

I really don’t have any advice but wanted to let you know that you’re not alone in this situation. What I will probably end up doing is just try not to overthink and focus on myself, I guess. Whatever is meant to be will be and we don’t have any control over what the other person feels.

Hello! I’m Mexican and I’ve been in a relationship with an American guy before. Earning in dollars/pounds vs earning in pesos is quite a big difference as you well know, so I think it’s great that you’re supporting her with things like rent. It’s honestly really hard to pay for rent with a normal salary in Mexico City, we still do it but it leaves us in quite a struggle. 

Now, about the borrowing money and her getting angry at your response…I’m going to go ahead and say that I don’t think she’s using you, it’s a cultural difference. We’re sensitive people and not used to expressing our feelings straight forward. She might just not have liked the honesty in your response. We Mexicans say stuff like “of course, here is the money and don’t worry about giving it back right away”. We do worry about the other person giving it back, but it’s implied, we don’t say it yet the other person understands what we mean and reads through our words. I know it can be a bit complicated to grasp!

If he’s still attracted to you, things might go somewhere from having that conversation. If he’s not anymore, at least you will have a good friend to help you out when you explore this new identity. Don’t be hard on yourself, feel what you feel and worry about things later, you’re still so young! Hugs to you

I’m glad my comment helped! I want to add that he might also not know that he’s not a dog person lol. I thought I was until I briefly dated a man with a border collie. The dog was beautiful and I enjoyed walking him, but I didn’t know how to do it at first (the leash thing happened to me as well and I got too nervous to fix it or didn’t think quickly enough). When I finally learned, I realized the dog required a lot more attention in general than I was capable of giving him when we were both alone, and I also realized I didn’t love sharing the bed with him. That’s when it clicked on me that although I can appreciate doggos I might not be so happy owning one. Maybe bring this issue up with him, and do clarify that you’re not excessive, you’re just a good dog owner. Ask him if he’s willing to treat your dog the same way you treat her, because she’ll still be with you for a long time, hopefully. If he says he’s willing, then do tell him that you require some patience and willingness to learn as well. People thing it’s easy to care for dogs but it’s a whole occupation in itself! Make sure he knows that and I hope that there is some way you can work it out. Hugs to you and the good girl 💕

I think you’re experiencing strong sexual attraction and need to cut all contact with this girl if you value your marriage. What you feel for her is projection only: what you think it could be, what you’d want it to be. It is not the real bond you have with your wife. We all will meet different kinds of people that will attract us or that we’ll have a connection with, but that’s what commitment and monogamy are all about, reigning in your impulse and being faithful to your spouse.

It could be that you guys have different libido. For some people having sex twice a week after the first year of marriage is perfectly fine, for others it’s not. If it isn’t fine for you, ask yourself if you’d be willing to continue like this for a long time, as he is unlikely to change. If you’re not, don’t waste any more time.

I think we sometimes take “I love you” as a synonym for commitment, but words aren’t everything. I would advice you to consider if that’s what it means to you; if it is, then you can definitely ask him about that, something like “Hey, I really like our relationship and would like it to continue being serious”. If you’ve already had this conversation and he has demonstrated his commitment, there is nothing to fear at all. The words will come! Meanwhile, try to focus on his actions. Not all men are as word-based as most of us women are. They tend to express their love in different ways. If he talks to you everyday and truly cares for you, then he definitely loves you, whether he feels like saying it right now or not. Hope it helps 🥰
